result.title: IMRF Small-Cap Growth Investment Management RFP
key_items: IMRF is soliciting qualified firms to provide domestic equity small cap growth investment management services.  The intent of the contractual relationship will be to establish an ongoing relationship between IMRF and the selected firm(s) for the purpo...
result.summary: IMRF seeks proposals from firms to manage domestic small-cap growth equity investments. It will not reimburse proposal preparation expenses and may reject any or all submissions. IMRF investment staff and its consultant will evaluate proposals; firms may be invited to present to the Investment Committee or Board of Trustees. Manager selection requires final Board approval. The goal is to establish an ongoing investment-management relationship with the selected firm or firms.

result.title: 1.3 QUIET PERIOD
key_items: The Quiet Period is the period of time beginning when the investment management RFP is issued and ends when the investment management firm(s) is(are) selected by the Board or the process is declared to be complete.

Respondents shall not contact IMRF Board members during the Quiet Period and should direct all questions and communications to the Director of Investments, Investment Department Manager, Executive Director or other contacts identified in this RFP.

Incumbent investment management firm respondents may communicate with IMRF Board members during the Quiet Period, but may not discuss the investment management search with the IMRF Board members during the Quiet Period.  The purpose of the Quiet Perio...
The Quiet Period will be posted to the IMRF website to prevent inadvertent violations by investment managers responding to the RFP.

IMRF Board members and members of the staff not directly involved in the investment manager(s) search shall refrain from communicating with the respondents regarding any product or service related to the search during the Quiet Period unless this comm...
An RFP respondent will be disqualified for violating the Quiet Period.
Offering or providing anything of value to the IMRF Board members and members of the staff is prohibited.
result.summary: The Quiet Period runs from issuance of the investment management RFP until the Board selects a firm or the process is declared complete. Respondents must direct questions and communications to the RFP-listed contacts, not Board members. Incumbent firms may communicate with Board members but may not discuss the search. These rules promote equal access, accurate and consistent communications, and a fair, diligent, efficient process; the period is posted on IMRF’s website. Board members and staff not involved in the search must not discuss related products or services with respondents, except during formal search site visits or interviews. Violations disqualify respondents, and providing anything of value to Board members or staff is prohibited.

result.summary: IMRF seeks capable investment managers who act in its best interests and recommend portfolio allocations, investment acquisitions, retention or dispositions, and changes to authorized investments. Managers select securities brokers, but may not use themselves or controlling, controlled, or affiliated entities without IMRF approval. Broker selection must follow fiduciary duties and IMRF’s minority-broker policy: at least 20% of brokerage for actively managed separate accounts should go to minority-, women-owned, and disabled broker-dealers; specified high-yield, small-cap international, micro-cap, and emerging-market managers must make best efforts, with the goal reviewed annually. Brokers should be chosen for favorable results, considering cost, reliability, execution capability, and useful research or services, in compliance with applicable laws. Managers must provide monthly written reports on portfolio composition and gross/net performance, outlook, significant changes, and explanations for benchmark variances. Further duties are set out in each manager’s agreement.

A qualified firm is an investment management firm registered as an investment adviser under the federal Investment Advisers Act of 1940 or a bank as defined in the federal Investment Advisers Act of 1940. The term of engagement shall commence on the effective date of the contract and shall continue until the date on which it is terminated by IMRF, or the Investment Manager, upon 30 days’ advance written notice to the other; provided, however, that at any time, without prior written notice, IMRF may orally direct the Investment Manager to cease its management activities with respect to the Fund, which direction shall be confirmed, in writing, as soon as practicable.
7.2 CRITERIA FOR THE EVALUATION OF PERFORMANCE
Performance shall be evaluated based upon successful execution of the services to be performed under the contract.

nodes.title: 10.3 FIRM INFORMATION
nodes.summary: The section requests comprehensive firm information, including organizational history, ownership and affiliations, services, business lines and revenues, offices and staffing, financial condition, regulatory status, litigation, conflicts, continuity plans, growth capacity, strategic changes, tax-exempt experience, staff board service, and diversity- or minority-owned status. It seeks personnel counts, experience and tenure, key staff biographies, senior departures and replacements, compensation, retention and training programs, and workforce diversity. Client-service questions cover account services, communication and meeting responsibilities, primary-contact availability and backup, and reporting. Compliance disclosures include assessment practices and findings, CCO reporting, regulatory inspections, sanctions, proceedings, fees and payments, internal controls, conflicts, risk-management leadership, trading restrictions and execution, trade allocation, side-by-side management, systems, brokerage allocation and diversity goals, and soft-dollar policies.

nodes.title: A. ORGANIZATIONAL SUMMARY
nodes.summary: A small-cap growth investment-management RFP requests firm and contact details, fiduciary classification, and a firm history covering organization, ownership, tax-exempt client services, capability development or acquisitions, prior names, affiliates, joint ventures, and recent material developments. It asks for an ownership/interrelationship chart, succession plans, office locations, functions, staffing, account-service assignments, business lines and revenue contributions, financial condition, recent ADV Part II, and business-continuity and disaster-recovery policies. Firms must describe growth objectives, client or asset capacity, portfolio-manager limits, resource expansion, and potential mergers, acquisitions, or spin-offs. The questionnaire also seeks regulatory oversight and registration dates; relevant litigation over the past five years and its status; broker-dealer status and trading; tax-exempt client work; staff board service, restrictions, and compensation; a conflict-of-interest policy and enforcement procedures; and qualification as a minority-, woman-, or disability-owned business under Illinois law.

nodes.title: B. FIRM PERSONNEL
nodes.summary: The section requests firm personnel information: employee counts by job function, average experience and tenure, with staff holding multiple roles counted under their main responsibility and explained in notes. It asks for biographies of principal officers, portfolio managers, analysts, and client service officers, identifying those responsible for the IMRF account, using a specified format for office, name, location, title, responsibilities, experience, education, and firm tenure. Firms must report senior departures over three years, reasons, timing, products, titles, tenure, and replacements; describe professional compensation and incentive awards; outline key-staff retention programs; and explain internal training for investment, compliance, and operations staff. A firm-wide diversity profile is also requested for full-time employees as of the latest available date, categorized by work group and demographic group. Other minorities include American Indian, Alaskan Native, and Asian/Pacific Islander; female minority employees are counted in their minority category, not as female or twice. The sample profile is dated December 31, 2008.

nodes.title: D. COMPLIANCE
nodes.summary: The RFP requests information on compliance assessment scope, timing, testing and frequency; the latest assessment and report; the chief compliance officer’s reporting line; regulator registration forms; the latest regulatory inspection and findings; sanctions in the past five years; pending or ongoing firm or affiliate litigation, investigations or proceedings; and investigations of principals. It also requires disclosure of direct and indirect service-related fees and payments, including dates, amounts and recipients, with updates when payments change. Governance questions cover internal controls and account conflicts and their mitigation. Trading questions address client-directed transaction restrictions, execution and best execution, equitable treatment and exceptions, trade allocation, side-by-side management, and back-office systems. Brokerage questions seek five-year percentages directed to minority-, women- and disabled-owned brokers, willingness to meet IMRF goals, and soft-dollar policies. The firm must also provide a biography or résumé of those responsible for overall risk management.

nodes.title: 10.4 PRODUCT INFORMATION
key_items: G. PORTFOLIO CHARACTERISTICS AND SECTOR WEIGHTINGS
nodes.summary: A product-information request covering: key dedicated personnel, roles, experience, portfolio responsibilities, and biographies; product name, inception date, objective, and benchmark rationale; assets and accounts by client type and investment vehicle, historical account losses and reasons, representative clients, and at least three references with relationship length and contact details; investment philosophy and its evolution, strategy, screening, portfolio construction, security trading decisions, manager structure, leverage and derivatives, model-portfolio discretion, client allocation, and meeting frequency; investment-risk controls, measurement, and stress testing; research methods, including fundamental, technical, and quantitative analysis; portfolio holdings, turnover, cash, fundamental characteristics, industry or sector allocations, and five-year capitalization-range distributions; and fee schedules, performance and other charges, account minimums, minimum annual fees and future changes, fee negotiability, and billing frequency.

nodes.title: 10.5 PERFORMANCE
nodes.summary: The section requests performance information: GIPS-compliant firms attach a product presentation; noncompliant firms provide a detailed 10-year (or firm-life) performance chart or table covering gross/net returns, benchmark returns, portfolio count, dispersion, and composite and firm assets. GIPS firms state years compliant and verified, identify the verifier, and provide a verification letter. Non-GIPS firms define the strategy composite and explain fee deductions, custom benchmarks, dispersion measures, interest-income treatment, cash allocation to carve-outs, subadvisers and periods, composite minimum assets, availability of return-calculation policies, and month-end valuation practices. Questionnaire appendices include organizational charts, SEC annual report or financial statements, business-continuity/disaster-recovery policies, conflict-of-interest policy and enforcement, and ADV Parts I and II. Exhibit A requires disclosure of compensation and expenses; names and addresses of the manager, related entities, owners above 7.5%, and executive officers; subcontractors and expected payments, with written notice of changes; and acknowledgment of Illinois Code provisions on fraud and prohibited contingent or placement fees and their penalties.

result.title: 3. The Investment Manager acknowledges that it is familiar with the provisions of Sections 1-135 and 1-145 of the Code, which read in their entirety as follows:
result.summary: The Investment Manager acknowledges familiarity with Illinois Code Sections 1-135 and 1-145. Section 1-135 makes knowingly falsifying retirement-system or investment-board records to defraud a Class 3 felony. Section 1-145 prohibits compensation contingent on influencing investment decisions or procuring investment services; violations are business offenses punishable by a fine of up to $10,000 and a three-year ban on such activities. Exhibit B is a sample letter requesting an annual certification under Public Act 095-0521 that an Illinois financial entity complies with the High Risk Home Loan Act to remain eligible for IMRF investment or deposits. It defines covered entities by reference to specified Illinois banking, credit union, savings and loan, mortgage lending, installment loan, and sales finance laws. The recipient is asked to indicate whether it qualifies, return the letter by fax or mail, and provide company name, signature, and date.
